# Appeal of Denial — Hip Arthroscopy (CPT 29914)

**Member:** Taylor Kimura
**Member ID:** W354999576
**Plan:** Cigna (Commercial/ACA), Kansas
**Denial date:** 2026-07-31
**Reference number:** POC-37F3AA304D-16940
**Governing policy:** Cigna CMM-314 Hip Surgery - Arthroscopic and Open Procedures V1.0.2026 (effective 2026-08-04)
Policy document: https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-314%20Hip%20Surg%20Arthro%20%26%20Open%20Proc_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.20.2026.pdf

Dear Cigna Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914), noted above. The denial letter states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I am asking Cigna to reconsider this decision using the complete records from my surgeon, Dr. Okafor, which I believe show that my condition matches the plan's own published criteria for this surgery.

## Why I believe the records meet Cigna's criteria

Cigna's policy states that femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) is medically necessary when certain criteria are met:

> "femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) is considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met:"

The policy further specifies:

> "◦ positive anterior impingement sign (i.e., groin-dominant hip pain with forced hip flexion, adduction, and internal rotation) ◦ limited passive hip internal rotation • Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration AND which must include the following (unless contraindicated):"

Here is how my records address each part of this:

**Positive impingement sign / groin-dominant pain.** My chart documents sharp anterior groin pain with sitting and pivoting, and positive provocative testing on the affected side. My exam also notes that my range of motion is limited by pain. I recognize the note does not use the exact phrase "limited passive hip internal rotation," and I am asking my surgeon's office to confirm and document this specific finding if it was measured, so the record speaks for itself on this point.

**Failure of non-surgical management for at least three months.** My records show:
- 16 weeks (2026-02-23 to 2026-06-15) of supervised physical therapy focused on core and hip stabilization with activity modification, 24 visits completed, documented in the physical therapy discharge note;
- NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief;
- a corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-21 that gave only 4 weeks of partial relief.

This is more than three months of provider-directed conservative treatment, and it did not resolve my symptoms.

**Imaging findings.** My MRI arthrogram from 2026-06-24 shows an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement and an alpha angle of 68 degrees. My joint space is preserved, and my Tonnis grade is 0.

Cigna's policy also states that hip arthroscopy for FAI is not medically necessary for certain other conditions:

> "Comprehensive Musculoskeletal Management Guidelines V1.0.2026 Arthroscopic or Open Hip Surgery for Femoroacetabular Impingement (FAI) Non-Indications CMM.JT.NI.314 v1.0.2026 Not Medically Necessary • Arthroscopic or open hip surgery for femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) is considered not medically necessary for ANY other indication or condition, including ANY of the following radiographic findings:"

The specific excluded radiographic findings were not included in the materials I was given, so I cannot address that list item by item. I would ask Cigna to confirm which, if any, of those excluded findings it believes apply to my imaging, since my preserved joint space and Tonnis grade of 0 do not appear to indicate advanced joint disease.

I am not requesting review under the synovectomy or "procedures not addressed elsewhere" sections of this policy, as my surgeon's request is specifically for arthroscopic treatment of femoroacetabular impingement with labral tear.

## What I am asking for

Because the denial cited incomplete documentation rather than a finding that I do not meet the medical necessity criteria, I am asking Cigna to review the complete clinical record described above — including the physical therapy discharge note, medication and injection history, exam findings, and MRI arthrogram report — and reverse the denial, or let me know specifically what additional documentation is needed.

My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary for my condition, and I would appreciate a full review of that documentation before a final decision is made.

## Deadline and how I am submitting this appeal

I understand this appeal must be received by **2027-01-27**. I am submitting it by logging in at my.cigna.com to find the plan's appeal form, and/or by calling the number on my member ID card (1-800-244-6224). If a specific mailing address was printed on my denial letter, I am also sending a copy there.

Thank you for reviewing this appeal.

Sincerely,

[Signature]
Taylor Kimura
Member ID: W354999576
[Date]
[Phone number]
[Email address]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
